problem: LLM-based VLN agents generate long chain-of-thought text autoregressively at every step, which accumulates large decision-stage latency, and much of the generated content (restatement, formatting, repeated state updates) is redundant.
motivation: Low per-step latency matters for practical embodied navigation. A token-composition analysis of step-wise CoT outputs shows about 47% is input restatement, about 9% formatting, and state updates are redundant across adjacent steps. So costly generation should be invoked only when needed, while action choice can be done by fast scoring.
key_idea: Replace per-step autoregressive action generation with batched Yes-logit verification over candidate actions, and call a generator for compact state evidence only when the verifier's normalized score entropy is high.
insight: Raw verification is extremely fast (0.05-0.08s/step) but nearly useless (SR 0.38%), so alignment training is essential. VPO lifts val-unseen SR from 0.38 to 37.25, and RFT adds to 39.63 SR and 51.26 OSR at a small SPL cost. Latency is driven by the verifier interface, not model size: with the same Qwen2.5-3B backbone, generator-based methods take 2.60-26.61s per step versus 0.080s for the verifier. Entropy triggering beats random and fixed-interval triggering, and failed episodes show higher entropy and more generator calls (both shown only in figures).
method: Verifier-first interface: for each candidate action (including STOP), builds a query from instruction, history, candidate-view captions and the action; scores it by the 'Yes' token logit in one batched forward pass; picks argmax.
Adaptive state-evidence generator: DeepSeek-V4-Pro produces a compact summary z_t from the same context; the summary is appended to the verifier queries and the actions are re-scored.
Entropy trigger: softmax over verifier scores, normalized entropy u_t; generator invoked if u_t > gamma, otherwise the verifier-only path is used.
VPO (static alignment): chosen-rejected action pairs built from annotated-path contexts and one-step-deviation recovery contexts; loss -log sigma(s+ - s- - m).

Step-level RFT (dynamic alignment): GRPO-style clipped objective on policy rollouts, with step reward = 1[distance decreases or new instruction landmark seen] - 0.2*revisit, and advantage = episode success advantage + 0.5*group-normalized step advantage, plus an entropy bonus.
Training setup: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with LoRA (rank 16, alpha 32) on one H100; VPO data from the R2R train split; RFT with N=4 rollouts, N_S=16, max 15 steps.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct verifier (LoRA fine-tuned); DeepSeek-V4-Pro as adaptive evidence generator (frozen, only in the collaboration path)
setting.training_data: R2R train split: VPO chosen-rejected pairs (annotated + recovery contexts), then RFT on policy-induced rollouts from R2R
setting.observation: Panoramic views converted to text captions of navigable candidate views (BLIP-style captioning)
setting.action_space: Discrete navigable candidate viewpoints plus STOP (nav graph), max 15 steps
setting.privileged: none at inference (reward signals such as graph distance and landmarks are used only in RFT training)

numbers.extra: verifier-only path; latency 0.08s/step; captions as input
numbers.evidence: Table 2 (main): R2R validation results, VerNav^r Val Unseen

numbers_note: Results with the entropy-triggered generator (full VerNav) on R2R SR/SPL are shown only in figures; only its latency (0.294s/step) is given in text. The 6.0-8.0 point SR gain from evidence was measured on a sampled val-unseen subset.
results: The verifier-only VerNav^r reaches 39.63 SR / 34.13 SPL on R2R val-unseen at 0.08s/step, about 12.3x faster than NavCoT (0.98s, 40.23 SR) with similar SR, and it has the best val-seen OSR/SR (53.48/43.10) among listed LLM-based methods. It trails DiscussNav (43 SR) and NavCoT on val-unseen SR/SPL.
limitations: Val-unseen SR (39.63) is still below NavCoT (40.23) and DiscussNav (43); only R2R is evaluated, with no continuous-environment or real-robot tests.

Relies on pre-generated text captions, so captioning cost is excluded from the latency comparison; the evidence generator is a large external model (DeepSeek-V4-Pro), and the entropy-triggered path raises latency to 0.294s.
Baseline SR values are copied from original papers while latency is re-measured, and RFT slightly lowers val-unseen SPL.
